# Retired- and static-instruction baselines for the bench corpus,
# checked against every run by scripts/ci-check-perf.
#
# FORMAT: metric  value  [tolerance%]. The metric key is
# <arch>/<benchmark>.<text|ir> — .text is the count of instructions in the
# emitted assembly, .ir the count of instructions actually retired.
#
# WHAT IS EXACT AND WHAT IS NOT. Every figure here repeats to the digit on a
# given commit EXCEPT the rows that hash string keys: core/map draws a
# per-process string-hash seed (#6194), which moves probe lengths, so a
# benchmark that builds a string-keyed map counts differently every run. That
# is `map_string.ir`, which does so directly, AND both `utf8_ingest_*.ir`
# rows, which do so through json_parse's `Map[string, JsonValue]` — the
# indirect case, and the one that went unclassified until a CI run happened to
# straddle the tolerance. Measured spreads over 15 runs of one binary:
# map_string 0.541%, utf8_ingest_unchecked 0.738%, utf8_ingest_validated
# 0.468%. map_string.ir keeps the 2% it was given for a 0.51% spread; the
# utf8_ingest rows carry 3% on the same reasoning at their larger spread, on
# BOTH arches, since the seed is drawn per process and not per ISA. A range
# grows with sample count, so these are floors, not ceilings — do not tighten
# a tolerance here against a handful of runs. Absolute endpoints are
# deliberately NOT quoted: they go stale the next time a line is re-banked for
# an unrelated reason, and a stale range reads as a real one. `map_int.ir` is
# exact — the seed is consulted for string keys only — and is deliberately
# left on the default so the two together show which half of a map regression
# moved.
#
# Everything else uses the 1% default, which flags a change of one part in a
# hundred. That is a significance threshold and not a noise floor: for those
# rows the count is exact, which `int_loop.ir` measuring identically over six
# runs is the control for.
#
# STRICT, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — perf.yml runs this comparison with
# FERN_CI_PERF_GATE_STRICT=1, so a row outside its tolerance fails the job
# whether it got worse or better. When a number moves on purpose, update it in
# the same PR; the job summary prints the corrected lines ready to paste. Keep
# the reason in the PR, not here.
#
# TWO ARCHITECTURES. An instruction count is not comparable across ISAs, so the
# keys are namespaced by arch and compared independently — and each job compares
# only its OWN namespace, so an x86_64 entry is not a missing measurement on the
# aarch64 runner.

# aarch64, the arch this project defaults to. The `.ir` half comes from the
# Perf workflow's own perf-aarch64 job, because no aarch64 host is available to
# the dev container — paste its block in verbatim. The `.text` half needs no
# such thing: it is a line count over `fern -target arm64-linux` output, which
# is host-independent, so a cross-compile from the dev container reproduces the
# runner's figure on EVERY row in this corpus and that is how the `.text` half
# is kept current. perf-aarch64 runs natively on ubuntu-24.04-arm, so the two
# are directly comparable. The three seeded rows — map_string.ir and both
# utf8_ingest_*.ir — carry the same tolerances their x86_64 twins do, for the
# same per-process hash seed, which is drawn per process rather than per ISA.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-09-04 (#7397) on the x86_64 `.text` half only, after the #4873
# containment bracket gained three field- and path-granular deaths: the three
# persistent-collection benchmarks lose bracket pairs (ordmap_insert -3.6%,
# pmap_insert -1.3%, pvec_with -1.2%). Every `.ir` row moved by less than its
# tolerance, so the trade is static size, not work.
#
# The two utf8_ingest `.text` rows were re-pinned in the same commit and
# credited to it. They are not its doing: the parent, a5cea3cd2, measures 31,424
# and 31,915 itself, so the +417 apiece was already on main. The values stand;
# the attribution did not. `map_int.text`, `map_string.text` and
# `map_probe_chain.ir` carry drift of the same kind — the last of them +1.35%,
# over its tolerance — and all three read identically at that parent, so they
# are left for whoever moved them rather than re-pinned here.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-09-05 (#8530) where the `.with` and constructor-reuse
# decisions moved into the IR: every row was measured twice on THIS corpus, on
# origin/main and on the change, and only the rows the pair disagreed on by
# more than their own tolerance were touched. Dynamically nothing got slower
# (pvec_with -10.5%, sort_inplace -7.8%, pmap_insert -5.9%); four `.text` rows
# grew 3-5%, which is the inline branch standing in for a call at every `.with`
# site. `array_with` and `record_update` are new, so their rows are first
# pins rather than re-pins — and their aarch64 `.ir` half is missing, because
# no aarch64 host measures it here; perf-aarch64 reports the two UNBASELINED
# for one run and its block goes in verbatim.
#
# Do NOT extrapolate an aarch64 figure from its x86_64 twin: the ratio is not
# constant. Over `.text` it runs from 0.85 (call_overhead) to 1.18
# (utf8_ingest_unchecked) — one ISA emitting fewer instructions than the other
# on one program says nothing about the next. A new benchmark reports as
# UNBASELINED here for one CI run, which is the gate saying "measured,
# recorded, not yet compared" — paste that run's block in rather than guessing.
